lesson.title: Containers from Zero, part 7: a small multi-container app
lesson.description: Build a notes app with a Python web service and a PostgreSQL database, start both with one compose.yaml, add notes with curl and a browser, and read the data inside the database. Then watch the notes vanish after down and up, and find out why.
lesson.tested: Ran the notes app on postgres:18-alpine with Compose v5.8.0 and Engine 29.10.1, 25 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: A web service and a database in one compose.yaml is a few lines; keeping the data needs one more, which part 8 adds.

steps.title: What the lab showed
steps.hint: IDs, addresses and times differ on your machine

items.what: The first `curl` came too early; in another run, `database unavailable` with `port 5432 failed: Connection refused` in the web log. Then `no notes yet`.
`HTTP/1.0 303 See Other`, then `1. First note`, `2. Buy coffee beans`.
`docker compose exec db psql -U notes -d notes -c ...` listed both rows.
`no notes yet`. `docker volume ls` showed two random names: the orphan `0b0882cc...` and the new `e75b303e...`.
`down -v` removed the attached volume; the orphan stayed until `docker volume rm` by name.

steps.note: Safety: publishes 127.0.0.1:8080; stop the part 6 project first. Cleanup deletes the database volumes and the notes. The password in compose.yaml is for this lab only. Undo with `docker compose down -v`, then `docker volume rm` the orphan by name.

commands.cmd: docker compose exec db psql -U notes -d notes -c 'SELECT id, body FROM notes;'
docker compose run --rm -e PGPASSWORD=notes-local-only db psql -h db -U notes -d notes -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM notes;'

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: How does `web` know where the database is?
exercises.a: From `DATABASE_URL`, `postgresql://notes:notes-local-only@db:5432/notes`. The host `db` is the service name, resolved on the project network.

exercises.q: Which environment variable must the PostgreSQL image have, and when do the `POSTGRES_*` variables take effect?
exercises.a: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, which must not be empty. The variables take effect only when the container starts with an empty data folder.

exercises.q: Why does the app answer `303 See Other` after a POST?
exercises.a: So the browser loads the list again with a plain GET to `Location: /`. Reloading the page then does not add the note twice.

exercises.q: Where does the database keep its files here, and what kind of storage is that?
exercises.a: Under `/var/lib/postgresql`, which the image declares as a volume. With no mount in compose.yaml, Docker gives it an anonymous volume.

exercises.q: What does the app do when the database cannot be reached?
exercises.a: It catches the error, logs `database error: ...`, and answers `503` with `database unavailable` instead of crashing.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose up -d --build` and `curl /notes.txt` at once, then again a few seconds later. What do you see, and why?
exercises.a: First a reset connection or `database unavailable`, then `no notes yet`. The app or PostgreSQL was not ready yet; `depends_on` only waits for running.

exercises.q: Add a note with `curl -i -X POST -d 'body=First note' ...`. Which status and header come back?
Compare the `PORTS` of `web` and `db` in `docker compose ps`. What does each mean?
exercises.a: `web`: `127.0.0.1:8080->8000/tcp`, published. `db`: `5432/tcp`, not published; only containers on `notes_default` can connect.

exercises.q: Run `docker volume ls`, `docker compose down`, `docker compose up -d`, `docker volume ls`. What changed, and where are your notes?
exercises.a: A second volume with a random name appeared and `/notes.txt` says `no notes yet`. The notes are in the first anonymous volume, which nothing mounts any more.

exercises.q: After `docker compose down -v`, run `docker volume ls`. Why is one volume still there?
exercises.a: `down -v` removes anonymous volumes attached to the project's containers. The orphan from the first run was attached to nothing.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You change the password in `DATABASE_URL` only. What does the web log show on the next request?
exercises.a: `password authentication failed for user "notes"`, and the app answers `503`. The two passwords must match.

exercises.q: You remove the `DATABASE_URL` line and run `up -d`. What happens to `web`?
exercises.a: It exits at once with `DATABASE_URL is not set`.

exercises.q: You run `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U notes notes` on your own machine. Does it reach the database?
exercises.a: No. Port 5432 is not published. Use `docker compose exec` or `docker compose run` instead.

exercises.q: You change `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in compose.yaml while the old database volume is still in use. Does the database password change?
exercises.a: No. The variables take effect only on an empty data folder; the existing database keeps its old password.
